title: Learned resonance analysis separates stiffness and damping feature patterns in coated microcantilevers
summary: Random-forest analysis of a large measured silicon-microcantilever dataset linked resonance frequency chiefly to effective modulus, thickness and geometry, while quality-factor variation emphasized coating thickness and effective modulus followed by surface descriptors. These are model-derived associations within the sampled wafers. Coating, roughness and material descriptors were correlated, so feature importance does not isolate causal dissipation mechanisms.
ai_technology: Random forest feature importance; extra-trees regression

source_review.scope: Read indexed original publisher Methods on measured endpoints, engineered features, RF importance and model families, plus feature-pattern Results, interpolation evaluation and limitations. Exact publisher front DOI/title/date matched current publisher-deposited Crossref canonical metadata; current relationship fields and indexed publisher notice context checked. Supplement and complete publisher HTML were not read.

evidence.tested: The study fabricated and measured 12,060 cantilevers across six wafers with uncoated silicon and four metal coatings. Endpoint-specific filtering retained 10,450–11,429 measurements. RF nonlinear feature importance distinguished features associated with fundamental resonance frequency from those associated with quality factor. Twelve regression families were compared using random within-design splits, with a 70:30 split used for later interpolation analyses.
evidence.unknown: Surface roughness was assigned per coating material and strongly correlated with surface category; several physical descriptors were nominal rather than device-specific measurements. Random splitting within sampled wafers tests interpolation, not unseen-material or independent-wafer generalization. Feature-importance rankings do not establish causal mechanisms, independently optimized devices or universal material laws.
evidence.ai_role: RF learned nonlinear associations between engineered geometry/surface descriptors and experimentally measured resonance endpoints, enabling the reported contrast in predictive feature patterns. Extra trees modeled the same measured response space.
